stumbles.why: "The two judges" are never introduced (humans? models?). Also, "legitimate prose" is ambiguous: it could mean the hits were false positives or real problems. The reason given (cells aren't sentences) suggests the hits were false positives, so the wording reads as contradictory.

stumbles.why: This flag is not explained elsewhere, and the text never says whether it exists in the same linter or how it is used.

stumbles.quote: It is meant for drafts that quote bad prose in italics on purpose and still need their tables skipped.
stumbles.why: The text never explains why such drafts need a flag that skips only tables. It also never says what "bad prose" means or what the linter flags, so the purpose of the whole tool is unclear.

stumbles.quote: With the flag set, the linter skips Markdown table rows and still scans the rest of the draft.
stumbles.why: The text never says what `declaude_lint.py` or the `declauding` skill is for, and it never defines "hits". A reader who has not seen the project cannot tell what is being linted.

stumbles.quote: every line that starts with `|` is blanked before scanning
stumbles.why: A table row indented or preceded by whitespace would not start with `|`. The text does not say whether those rows are skipped. It also does not say how table separator rows and tables without leading pipes are handled.

point: The PR adds a `--skip-tables` flag to the declauding linter. The flag blanks lines that start with `|`, so line numbers stay correct. It is a narrower alternative to `--skip-quoted`, and the PR justifies it with a scan where most table hits were judged not to be real problems.
